summary: Rode 60.9 miles from Vega State Park down to Grand Junction, CO, leaving the Rockies. A steep unofficial gravel shortcut off I-70 took about 20 minutes to push up, and the team swam in the Colorado River before hosts Greg and Steph fed them.
slept_at: Greg and Steph's renovation house, Grand Junction, CO (Warmshowers host)
contacts: Greg and Steph, Grand Junction, CO (hosts; vegan burritos, fridge of fruit and electrolyte drinks)
planning_notes: Near Grand Junction, a shortcut off I-70 turns into a very steep ~0.2 mi climb that took ~20 min to push a bike up; a gravel road exists at the top, so use the mapped route.
The I-70 shoulder near Grand Junction is busy and full of debris; use the bike paths into town instead.
Gravel on the day before knocked out several water bottles; secure bottle cages.
Colorado River swim stop near Palisade/Corn Lake is a good cooldown, but the current is strong.
A budget and spending discussion at the Milky Way ice cream shop in Palisade ran over two hours; schedule money talks outside rest stops.

summary: Rode 114.1 miles from Grand Junction, CO to Moab, UT, the second-longest day of the trip, through heat, headwinds, and I-70 with no services for 40-50 miles. A rider's tire trouble created an unofficial rest stop, and the team arrived in Moab after 8:45pm.
slept_at: Airbnb in Moab, UT (arranged by Sarah's parents)
contacts: Jennifer and Mike, Sarah's parents, Moab, UT (booked the Airbnb and cooked dinner)
planning_notes: Signs on I-70 warn of no services for 40-50 miles after leaving Grand Junction; carry all food and water for that stretch.
Carry a spare tube and patch kit; tire trouble on the Grand Junction-to-Moab road left one rider stranded while the others waited.
Canyon section into Moab has a bike path that is safe and car-free for the final ~10 miles; the 2-mile climb at the end is worth knowing about.
A Colorado River dip near Moab was much-needed relief in the afternoon heat.
A 114-mile day needed a 6:30am start and still ran until 8:45pm; for long days, plan dinner timing with hosts in advance.

summary: Rest day in Moab hosted by Sarah's parents: cinnamon rolls, a bike shop and bookstore run, a Colorado River rafting trip, a sunset hike to Delicate Arch in Arches National Park, and a group dinner at an Italian restaurant.
slept_at: Airbnb in Moab, UT (arranged by Sarah's parents)
contacts: Jennifer and Mike, Sarah's parents, Moab, UT (Airbnb for two days)
Jonah, rafting guide, Moab, UT (Colorado River trip; company name not given)
planning_notes: Colorado River rafting out of Moab with a guide is a good group rest-day activity; the trip saw bald eagles and an otter den.
Delicate Arch gets crowded at sunset; arriving earlier or later is much quieter.
Spoke on Center (Italian, Moab) has a very big menu, so decide on shared plates before you sit down.

summary: Second Moab rest day: a six-mile out-and-back hike to The Needles viewpoint in Canyonlands in midday heat, then a hot tub and cornhole night at the condo complex. The hike was harder than the team expected.
slept_at: Airbnb in Moab, UT (arranged by Sarah's parents)
contacts: Jennifer, Sarah's mom, Moab, UT (cooked a lox bagel breakfast and a flank steak dinner)
planning_notes: The Canyonlands Needles hike is about 1.5 hours' drive from Moab and 6 miles out and back; start early, since noon in July was very hot and the team went through lots of water.
Walking hikes can be more tiring than riding for some riders after a long bike trip; plan a light day after a hike.

summary: Left Moab after a disorganized morning and a fire sandwich stop. Ramona's rear derailleur cable snapped at rest stop 2, so the driver took her to a Moab bike shop and then drove to the Green River campground after the riders arrived.
slept_at: Green River campground, UT (had electricity and signal)
contacts: Unnamed mechanic at a Moab bike shop who repaired Ramona's bike
planning_notes: The highway from Moab toward rest stop 2 is high-speed (cars around 80 mph) with almost no shoulder; a left turn across it is very hard to make safely, so pass the turn and U-turn well down the road.
Green River has no bike shops; the next ones are in Moab, so fix any mechanical issues there before heading west.
Rural Utah gas is expensive; only buy what you need to reach the next town.
A wacky alien-themed gas station on this route had water refills, so know your water stops.
Taking a dirt-road detour to avoid the highway added about 30 miles of self-supported riding in the heat; plan support for it.

summary: Rode 94.4 miles from Green River State Park to Capitol Reef National Park, with ten climbs, heat, and dehydration. The team arrived at the campground just in time for a $25-per-person dinner, and raccoons stole the bagels from camp that night.
slept_at: Capitol Reef National Park campground, UT
contacts: Spokes 2019 alumni (funded the team's dinner at $25 per person)
planning_notes: Capitol Reef campground has no showers; washing in the bathroom sinks worked.
Raccoons got into open food and bagels at the campsite overnight; keep food sealed and in the car.
The restaurant near Capitol Reef closes at 9pm; with 10 miles left at 6:30pm, call ahead about closing times.
Electrolyte packets ran low; gallon batches of fruit-punch electrolyte drink carried the team through heat.
Bull's Market is a store-based rest stop on this route, so you can restock there.

summary: Capitol Reef rest day: the team worked from the visitor center Wi-Fi, ran errands, took a scenic drive, and saw very dense stars at the campground. The national park grocery was expensive, and the sunset hike missed the sunset.
slept_at: Capitol Reef National Park campground, UT
planning_notes: The Capitol Reef visitor center has Wi-Fi but little workspace; bring a plan for working on rest days.
Park grocery prices are high; buy supplies before entering the park.

summary: Charles drove a long day after packing the campsite alone, which made him miss rest stop 1 and pick up Tian, who could not finish the climb. Headwinds, wildfire smoke, a long gravel ascent, and a bumpy gravel descent left riders exhausted, and the team reached a pastor's house in Escalante after dusk.
slept_at: Pastor's house, Escalante, UT (church host)
contacts: Pastor hosting in Escalante, UT (house with dogs)
planning_notes: The gravel descent toward Escalante is very bumpy and tiring; take breaks, and Greta fell backward while stopping on it.
Headwinds were loud enough to hear from inside the car; start early when the forecast is windy.
Rest stop 3 on this route is a treeless, windy pullover with no shade; bring shade or keep the stop short.
There is little or no cell signal around Capitol Reef, so agree on meeting points and check-in times between driver and riders.
Packing a campsite alone as driver took about two hours; share packing chores so the driver can leave on time.

summary: Rode 51.5 miles from Escalante to Bryce Canyon National Park over two climbs, a viewpoint, and a cafe stop, arriving before dark. A fire ban began at midnight at the campground, so the team had dinner and a fire first.
slept_at: Bryce Canyon National Park campground, UT
contacts: Escalante hosts and their dogs (names not given)
planning_notes: The Bryce campground fire ban began at midnight on the night the team arrived; check fire restrictions before planning a campfire.
Riding in a peloton cut the effort into headwinds on the first climb.
The cafe near Bryce has an ice machine outside, which is handy for refilling water.
Tubeless sealant fixed a puncture but left a blob in the tire; check the tire after sealing.
Greta made about eight sandwiches in the morning for the team; batch-making lunches saves time each day.

summary: Bryce Canyon rest day: a hike on the Navajo Loop with steep grades near the end, followed by camp lunch and a group dinner of Ramona's soup and potstickers. The camp restaurant was too expensive and the pizzeria had a long wait.
slept_at: Bryce Canyon National Park campground, UT
planning_notes: The camp restaurant at Bryce is expensive and the pizzeria has a long wait; plan to cook at camp.
Navajo Loop has steep grades toward the end; it is a good rest-day hike but harder than it looks after biking.
Learning festival supplies were shipped in an Amazon box and kept at the campsite.

summary: Zion rest day: a team hike up Angels Landing using the shuttle and a permit, with lunch on top and a wade in the river. The Zion laundromat was closed, so the team drove about 20 miles to a Hurricane, UT laundromat late at night.
slept_at: Robin's house, Zion area, UT (host)
contacts: Robin, host near Zion, UT (cooked multi-dish dinners for the team)
planning_notes: Angels Landing uses a lottery permit system; the team got two permits, and the rangers check permits at the station before the last mile.
The Angels Landing trail starts with steep, narrow switchbacks for about 1.5 miles; biking up or down that trail is not practical.
Zion Park Laundry was closed (sign said closed for the next month); the nearest open laundromat was in Hurricane, UT, more than 20 miles away.
Hoodoo's General Store gave free all-day parking when riders spent about $25 on snacks.
Do laundry before rest days; the team ran low on clean clothes and had to rush.

summary: The shortest mileage day (29.75 miles) but the largest single climb of the trip, up Kolob Terrace Road to Lava Point Campground. A sharp piece of metal on the road slashed Ishaq's new tire, and the team washed in cold, muddy Kolob Reservoir because the campground had no showers.
slept_at: Lava Point Campground, UT (no showers, no service)
planning_notes: Kolob Terrace Road has the largest single climb of the trip with very steep sections; start early.
Sharp debris on the road slashed a tire; check tires before the climb and carry a spare tube or tire.
Lava Point Campground has no showers and no cell service; the only service in the area is at the Lava Point viewpoint.
Kolob Reservoir water is very cold and the shore is muddy, so it is only a rough wash.
Wind at the campground blew things around, including a tent into the forest; stake tents and secure gear.

summary: Rode 89.5 miles from Lava Point to Milford, UT. Tian was badly hurt in a fall on a gravel descent, and the team used phone screenshots for navigation because the route had not been loaded before the campground, which had no service.
slept_at: Mt. View Church, Milford, UT (church host)
contacts: Mt. View Church, Milford, UT (church host)
planning_notes: Load routes onto bike computers before leaving a no-service campground such as Lava Point; phone screenshots worked as a backup.
A gravel descent just after Lava Point caused a serious fall for Tian; ride gravel descents slowly and within control.
Ishaq's rear derailleur broke at rest stop 4, near a bike shop; check drivetrain and tire condition before long climbs.
Tailwinds came in the last miles into Milford and were a welcome break from headwinds.

summary: Tian, still recovering from a gravel-descent fall, rode as a passenger while the team rode 83.4 miles from Milford, UT to Baker, NV. Cross-winds made one rider take an hour to cover 7 miles, and the team stayed at a Baker church with no kitchen and a clogged bathroom.
slept_at: Baker, NV church (church host; no kitchen, clogged bathroom)
contacts: Baker, NV church host (name not given)
planning_notes: In Baker, NV the church host has no kitchen and a clogged bathroom; showers are at a gas station in town.
Cross-winds in the Milford-to-Baker stretch were brutal; flat roads with mirages felt endless, so plan for slow miles.
A laundry bag of clothes was missed in a late-night wash; label laundry bags or keep a running list.
Deep-cleaning bikes the night before loosened brakes; check brakes after any bike cleaning.
The driver waited 40 minutes at rest stop 3 for a rider; a passing motorist offered food, so keep extra food in the van.

summary: Sarah had a serious allergic reaction after eating a muffin made with almond flour at a Baker, NV cafe; Greta gave her an EpiPen, and she was driven to urgent care about 45 minutes away. The rest of the team rode 61.7 miles on Highway 50 to Ely, NV and stayed at a high school.
slept_at: White Pine County High School, Ely, NV (school host, cafeteria)
contacts: Hosts at White Pine County High School, Ely, NV (ordered pizza for the team)
planning_notes: Ask about ingredients at cafes and bakeries: a muffin at the Baker cafe contained almond flour; carry an EpiPen and know the nearest urgent care.
The nearest hospital with urgent care from Baker was about 45 minutes away; plan a driver for any medical trip.
Highway 50 across Nevada has no viable coffee or food stops between Baker and Ely; carry food and water.
Carl Jr's in Ely had cookies-and-cream milkshakes; the McDonald's ice cream machine was broken.

summary: Learning festival day in Ely, NV at the library across from the middle school, with about 12 kids and one retired special-education teacher who observed. The afternoon was spent on 3D print troubleshooting and a team dinner at the high school.
slept_at: White Pine County High School, Ely, NV
learning_festival: Ely library, across from the middle school, Ely, NV: about 12 kids with one adult observer; ran half in a conference room and half on the lawn; kids were into math and dirt biking
contacts: Retired special-education teacher who joined the festival (name not given), Ely, NV
planning_notes: The Ely library is a good learning-festival site: it has a lawn, a pond, and a conference room; arrive when it opens.
A corrupted SD card delayed the 3D prints into the next day; bring backup SD cards and test prints early.
The Ely grocery store is large and well stocked; restock there before heading west.

summary: Rode 69.8 miles along Highway 50 from Ely to Eureka, NV over Robinson Pass (7,607 ft) and several summits. The team shuttled 18 miles north to Diamond Valley Baptist Church, and the car nearly ran out of gas on the way.
slept_at: Diamond Valley Baptist Church, about 18 miles north of Eureka, NV (church host)
contacts: Diamond Valley Baptist Church, near Eureka, NV (church host; padded pews, one shower in the girls' bathroom)
planning_notes: Highway 50 in Nevada has long climbs: Robinson Pass (7,607 ft), Little Antelope and Pancake summits, and Pinto summit (7,376 ft); the shoulder is narrow, so riding in pairs is hard.
The Diamond Valley Baptist Church is about 18 miles off route north of Eureka; the church has a single shower in the girls' bathroom.
The car had about 20 miles of gas left when the nearest station was 15 miles away and closing; fill up in Eureka before heading north.
Riding with a phone call or a podcast helped the long climbs pass; a rider talked on the phone for 30-40 minutes on one climb.

summary: The last learning festival, in Fallon, NV, ran for 6 to 8 kids per group, the team's tenth time running it. A soda bottle with baking soda and vinegar cracked and sprayed a student, and the team slept on a Youth Center teen room couch.
slept_at: Youth Center teen room, Fallon, NV (couch)
learning_festival: Youth Center, Fallon, NV: last learning festival, 6-8 kids per group, team's tenth run of the program; chemistry demo with baking soda and vinegar
contacts: Youth Center staff, Fallon, NV (hosted the team and its kitchen)
planning_notes: The Youth Center teen room is usable as sleeping space, and its industrial kitchen is open for breakfast.
The baking soda and vinegar demo cracked a soda bottle that sprayed a kid; use goggles and check bottles before the demo.
A scuffle broke out between kids; keep adults close during group activities.
Kids got distracted by balloons; plan hands-on activities with a short break between sections.

summary: Ruth drove the day, using a spray bottle to wake riders and setting up a float station with ice cream and soda at a rest stop. The team rode 96.8 miles from Fallon, NV to South Lake Tahoe, CA, entered California, and stayed with Warmshowers hosts after dark.
slept_at: Warmshowers hosts Natasha and Dan, South Lake Tahoe, CA
contacts: Natasha and Dan, Warmshowers hosts, South Lake Tahoe, CA (grilled dinner for the team)
planning_notes: Riders finishing after dark need bike lights; the driver had to go back for lights, so carry spare lights in the van.
A float station with ice cream and soda at a rest stop boosted morale on a long day.
Insomnia Cookies in South Lake Tahoe is open late for a post-ride snack.
The drive from Carson City to Genoa is scenic; Genoa was founded in 1851.

summary: Rode 88.8 miles from South Lake Tahoe to Placerville, CA with about 6,700 ft of climbing and 11,000 ft of descent. The driver brought groceries, fruit, and smoothies, and a one-lane highway closure for log trucks held riders for about 20 minutes near the top.
slept_at: Church in Placerville, CA (church host)
contacts: Church host in Placerville, CA (name not given)
planning_notes: A highway section near the top of the last climb had one lane and a flagger for log trucks; expect a wait of about 20 minutes.
Sly Park Recreation Area (rest stop 5) charges vehicles a fee, but the access road is free for bikes.
The driver's groceries (watermelon, fruit, family-size smoothie) were a major hit at rest stop 2; ask for food planning in advance.
A bug flew into a rider's eye on the long descent; keep glasses on and pull over to rinse if needed.

summary: South Lake Tahoe rest day: a 28-hole mini golf round that took about four hours, then a beach rock concert with bike valet and a late bowling plan. Food prices at the beach were high.
slept_at: Dan and Natasha's house, South Lake Tahoe, CA (Warmshowers)
planning_notes: The beach concert had a bike valet and high food prices (8 dumplings for $15); bring cash and set a budget.
A 28-hole mini golf round took about four hours with a big group; plan a shorter course for time.
South Lake Tahoe nights are very cold at elevation; close windows before bed.

summary: A team scavenger hunt with side quests turned a 54.2-mile ride from Placerville into a long day: the first rest stop, 19.4 miles out, came about five hours after the start. The team swam at a park lake and reached Ray and Judy's home in Sacramento in the evening.
slept_at: Ray and Judy's home, Sacramento, CA (host)
contacts: Ray and Judy, Sacramento, CA (hosts; pasta dinner with yard vegetables)
planning_notes: Side quests ate the day: the first rest stop took five hours; set a time limit for side tasks and keep the riding schedule.
A park lake along the route had a good swimming spot for a break.
A car wash near a gas station was useful for rinsing bikes.

summary: The team split into a Six Flags group that left early and a regular group that rode 74.9 miles from Sacramento to Benicia, CA through Davis, Dixon, and Vacaville. They rode the last stretch after dark on an interstate service road and arrived at 10:30pm.
slept_at: Host home in Benicia, CA (host name not given)
planning_notes: The last stretch into Benicia after dark ran on an interstate service road with headlights in the eyes and a confusing route; start earlier to finish in daylight.
The van could not shuttle riders because of its planned schedule; have a plan for dark arrivals.
The bike path from Sacramento to Davis runs along the highway and is busy with commuters in the morning; the ride is flat.
Davis has a cluster of good stops (a Korean bingsu dessert shop and a newspaper shop), but time disappears there fast.
Dixon fruit market had watermelon juice, bread, and cheese for a quick resupply.

summary: Final San Francisco day: the team packed the van one last time, then toured Ghirardelli Square and Japantown and ate a Thai dinner, the team's final supper. Greta left at 6am for a flight, and the rest rode autonomous taxis back to the house.
slept_at: House in San Francisco, CA (arrangement not stated)
planning_notes: A round-trip car rental (rather than a one-way) let the team drive the van back east instead of shipping bikes and camping gear; this made the end logistics much easier.
Consolidating boxes and reorganizing the van made food easy to grab; it carried two bikes inside plus three on the rack.
Autonomous taxis are available in San Francisco for getting around.

summary: After the team's flights left in the morning, the last three riders drove 426 miles north along the coast, stopping at Humboldt Redwoods, a Pacific beach, and Redwoods National Park. They arrived at Humbug Mountain State Park, OR after dark.
slept_at: Humbug Mountain State Park campground, OR (arrived after dark)
planning_notes: The team arrived after dark on a 400+ mile drive; plan an arrival before dark on long driving days.
Humboldt Redwoods and Redwoods National Park are a worthwhile scenic detour on the coast route north from San Francisco.
Spokes belongings were delivered to Cambridge after the trip; plan end-of-trip returns of gear before the final ride.
